subject: MAP & evaluation cadence — proposed rebaseline and exec ask
messages:
From: Dana Ruiz <dana.ruiz@luminahealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@luminahealth.com>
Date: 2027-11-03T08:23:00-08:00
Subject: MAP & Eval timeline for Redwood POC

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo — the team was impressed with the latency profile. We're starting to formalize the evaluation plan but are hitting a couple of internal blockers that may push our acceptance date out: procurement needs an updated SOW, and Security asked for a SOC 2 evidence packet before running any production data.

Can you share a short risk log and proposed MAP that shows what a 3-week vs 6-week slip looks like (impact on rollout milestones, what we can gate on, and any options for temporary dedicated capacity)? Procurement also asked for an indicative cost impact if we need reserved capacity for the trial.

Attaching our internal evaluation checklist so you can map items to the plan.

Thanks,
Dana Ruiz
Director, Clinical Data Integration
LuminaHealth

Attachment: Lumina_Eval_requirements.pdf (PDF)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dana Ruiz <dana.ruiz@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@luminahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-11-03T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP & Eval timeline for Redwood POC

Dana — thanks for the checklist. I've sketched a short risk register and two rebaseline options (3-week / 6-week) and mapped acceptance gates to deliverables. High level summary below; MAP_v1 attached.

Quick risk summary (from risk_log_lumina.csv):
- Procurement delay (procurement needs updated SOW): impact +5 to +14 days to start of production validation if contract edits exceed 48 hours.
- Security evidence lag (SOC2 artifacts): blocking for any production-like data; mitigation: scoped synthetic data test for functional eval (acceptance gate: feature parity on synthetic dataset).
- Integration sprint shift: engineering dependency with Lumina ETL team could add +7 days if integration slot moved.

Option A — 3-week rebaseline (recommended if procurement signs within 7 days):
- New internal target: 2027-12-01 acceptance window
- Acceptance gates: 1) Synthetic data functional pass; 2) Minimal SOC2 evidence provided; 3) Integration smoke test
- Cost impact: no dedicated capacity initially; we can offer a 20% credit if acceptance slips beyond the new date

Option B — 6-week rebaseline (if procurement/SEC confirm longer lead times):
- New internal target: 2027-12-22 acceptance window
- Acceptance gates: full SOC2 evidence or SOC2-equivalent attestation; production-mirroring dataset window; extended integration validation
- Cost impact: recommend Reserved Trial (1x Dedicated pool) to ensure stable latency — estimated incremental cost: ~$9,200 for the trial period (prices indicative)

Ask: can procurement/exec confirm whether they can sign the updated SOW within the next 5 business days? If not, we recommend Option B and I will escalate for a one-time credit and short-term dedicated capacity to protect performance during validation.

I've attached: Lumina_MAP_v1.xlsx and risk_log_lumina.csv.

Cheers,
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
mateo@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0142

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-11-04T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: MAP & Eval timeline for Redwood POC — escalation recommendation

Ben / Mateo — forwarding the thread and our proposed options. Procurement is likely to take at least a week to route the SOW internally; Security may require the SOC2 artifacts which would push to Option B.

Recommendation (we should move quickly):
1) Approve a provisional 3-week rebaseline (Option A) to buy breathing room for Lumina while procurement works the SOW.
2) If procurement cannot sign within 5 business days, auto-fallthrough to Option B and authorize a one-time reserved trial credit (we can propose a 15% credit against the dedicated trial cost).
3) Notify Legal and CS so they can prepare the amended SOW and a short addendum covering the limited dedicated pool for the trial.

I'll take point on the credit ask and prep the language — Mateo, please confirm the reserved-trial SKU and the exact dollar impact so Ben can sign off.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Director, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, security@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-11-05T15:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP & Eval timeline for Redwood POC — agreed rebaseline and next steps

Dana / Jordan / Lumina procurement team — thanks for the transparency. We want to keep momentum and will accept a provisional 3-week rebaseline (Option A) with the following conditions:

1) Agreed provisional acceptance window: target acceptance 2027-12-01; hard deadline for re-evaluation 2027-12-15.
2) If procurement cannot return a signed SOW within five business days (by 2027-11-10), Lumina agrees to move to the Option B cadence and Redwood will provision a Reserved Trial pool. We will apply a one-time 15% trial credit to the dedicated trial cost as outlined by Marissa.
3) Acceptance gates: a) synthetic-data functional pass, b) integration smoke test, c) submission of SOC2 artifact package (or SOC2-equivalent attestation). Synthetic-data validation can proceed earlier; we'll enable test tokens for your engineers.
4) Next actions: Mateo will circulate MAP_v2 (milestone dates + ownership) and Marissa will ring-fence the credit approval. Legal will prepare an SOW addendum and an expedited DocuSign for signature.

Attachments: MAP_v2_Lumina.docx (contains new milestone dates); DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/to/updated_sow

We remain committed to the timeline — reach out directly if you want a quick sync to walk through the acceptance gates.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
ben@redwoodinference.com | +1 650-555-0199
